name: MonarchRoadmap
title: Roadmap
wrapsNative: MonarchGanttTimeline with undated: .row, the quarter zoom and the roadmap's names (and through it ScrollView(.horizontal) with Canvas drawing, LongPressGesture sequenced before DragGesture with sensoryFeedback, accessibilityActions, Menu with an inline Picker, Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented), and Form with DatePicker in a sheet)
summary: Projects over months and quarters, grouped by initiative, with progress, the health last reported in words, milestones and dependencies between projects, on the Gantt timeline.
whenToUse: To give leads a long-range view of projects across teams: when each runs, how far along it is, what was last reported and which projects block others. Pass onChange only where people really replan on this screen.
whenNotToUse: To schedule individual tasks by dragging use MonarchGanttTimeline directly. For a status-only overview without dates use a List of rows with MonarchStatusBadge.
api: init(_ items: [MonarchRoadmapItem], state: Binding<MonarchGanttTimelineState>? = nil, groups: [MonarchRoadmapGroup] = [], dependencies: [MonarchGanttTimelineDependency] = [], milestones: [MonarchGanttTimelineMilestone] = [], zoomLevels: [MonarchGanttTimelineZoom] = [.month, .quarter, .year], today: Date? = Date(), showsToolbar: Bool = true, labels: MonarchRoadmapLabels = MonarchRoadmapLabels(), timelineLabels: MonarchGanttTimelineLabels = MonarchGanttTimelineLabels(), onChange: (@MainActor (MonarchRoadmapItem, MonarchGanttTimelineDates) -> Void)? = nil, onOpen: (@MainActor (MonarchRoadmapItem) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder toolbarActions: () -> ToolbarActions)

init(_ items: [MonarchRoadmapItem], state: Binding<MonarchGanttTimelineState>? = nil, groups: [MonarchRoadmapGroup] = [], dependencies: [MonarchGanttTimelineDependency] = [], milestones: [MonarchGanttTimelineMilestone] = [], zoomLevels: [MonarchGanttTimelineZoom] = [.month, .quarter, .year], today: Date? = Date(), showsToolbar: Bool = true, labels: MonarchRoadmapLabels = MonarchRoadmapLabels(), timelineLabels: MonarchGanttTimelineLabels = MonarchGanttTimelineLabels(), onChange: (@MainActor (MonarchRoadmapItem, MonarchGanttTimelineDates) -> Void)? = nil, onOpen: (@MainActor (MonarchRoadmapItem) -> Void)? = nil) where ToolbarActions == EmptyView

struct MonarchRoadmapItem: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(id: String, label: String, start: Date? = nil, end: Date? = nil, groupID: String? = nil, progress: Double? = nil, progressText: String? = nil, health: MonarchRoadmapHealth? = nil, tone: MonarchTone? = nil) }
struct MonarchRoadmapGroup: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(id: String, label: String, start: Date? = nil, end: Date? = nil, health: MonarchRoadmapHealth? = nil) }
enum MonarchRoadmapHealth: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case onTrack, atRisk, offTrack, notReported }

struct MonarchRoadmapLabels: Sendable { init(health: (@Sendable (MonarchRoadmapHealth) -> String)? = nil, count: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, meta: (@Sendable (_ first: String, _ second: String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: items
options.description: The projects: id, label, start and target dates (neither makes a row that says "No dates"), groupID, progress from 0 to 1, progressText such as "8/20", health (nil writes none, .notReported writes "No health reported") and tone (nil takes it from health).

options.name: state
options.description: The first visible day, the zoom, chart or list. nil keeps the state inside the roadmap, which opens at the quarter zoom (nine months visible); a binding starts from the app's value.

options.name: groups
options.description: Initiatives, themes or teams as heading rows, in order. Each heading says how many projects it has and its health; a group with dates shows a thin span. Projects without a known group follow the groups.

options.name: dependencies
options.description: Links between projects, drawn as arrows and written as "Depends on" in the list.

options.name: milestones
options.description: Dated checkpoints: on a project's row with itemID, otherwise in a lane under the header.

options.name: zoomLevels
options.description: The zoom levels offered in the toolbar's zoom menu.

options.name: today
options.description: Any time on the day of the today line, read in the environment's calendar; nil hides the line and disables Today. Pass a fixed date in tests and previews.

options.name: showsToolbar
options.description: Shows the toolbar: Today, Earlier, Later, the visible range, the zoom menu, the chart and list switch and toolbarActions.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the roadmap's own strings: the health words, the group count and the joiner of a heading's second line.

options.name: timelineLabels
options.description: Replacements for the timeline's strings. The chart is named "Roadmap" and the row header says "Project" unless timeline or rowHeader is given here; every other value is passed through.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Makes dates editable (touch and hold then drag, arrow keys, VoiceOver actions, the date sheet in the list) and is called with the roadmap project and its new dates. Without it the roadmap is read-only.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Makes each bar and list row a button that calls back with the roadmap project.

options.name: toolbarActions
options.description: Extra controls at the end of the toolbar, such as a team filter.

states.name: read only
states.description: The default. Bars have no drag, no key handling and no VoiceOver actions; with onOpen they are still buttons that open the project.

states.name: editable
states.description: With onChange, everything the timeline offers to change dates, and onChange receives the roadmap project, not a timeline row.

states.name: health
states.description: On track, at risk, off track or no health reported is written in words on the row heading's second line, after the progress text; at risk tints the bar warning and off track danger.

states.name: no health tracked
states.description: With health nil nothing is written about health and the bar keeps the accent colour.

states.name: no dates
states.description: A project without dates stays in its group as a row that says "No dates" instead of moving to an Unscheduled section.

states.name: out of view
states.description: A project outside the visible window says "Ended …" or "Starts …" on its row.

states.name: list
states.description: The list view writes each project's dates, length, progress, progress text and health and its dependencies.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no items the roadmap shows its toolbar and the chart header with no rows; show MonarchEmptyState instead when the app has nothing planned.

appearance: As MonarchGanttTimeline: on the surface colour with subtle lines, group headings on the subtle background. Bars are a light tint of the accent with the accent's solid fill as outline and progress strip; at-risk bars use the warning tone and off-track bars the danger tone. The second line of each heading (progress text, health, count) is in the muted text colour. Dark and both high-contrast themes swap in their own roles.
platformNotes: Matches Android's MonarchRoadmap names and options in Swift form: dates are Date values read as calendar days in the environment's calendar (Android uses UTC day keys, the web ISO strings), groupID instead of groupId, health cases in lower camel case, state is an optional Binding<MonarchGanttTimelineState> (nil keeps it inside, at the quarter zoom) instead of a remembered state object, the toolbar Boolean is showsToolbar, there is no timeZone parameter (the environment's timeZone is used) and no icon parameters (the toolbar arrows are SF Symbols from MonarchCalendarToolbar). The web shows health as a Badge with a dot next to the progress text; MonarchGanttTimeline takes its row meta as a plain String, so iOS, like Android, writes the progress text and the health word on one muted line ("8/20 · On track") with no dot or badge colour: the words carry the meaning, the bar tint repeats it. The web's hidden no-health dash becomes the visible words "No health reported" (.notReported), and the web's undefined versus null becomes nil (nothing written) versus .notReported. The item title is a plain label, not a view slot. Progress is 0 to 1 instead of 0 to 100, and onChange returns nothing (the web's promise and rollback become the app passing new items back). The web's accent tone is tone nil, because MonarchTone has no accent case; an app cannot force the accent colour on an at-risk or off-track project. defaultZoom becomes the state parameter. Everything else (sideways-only chart scrolling, touch and hold to drag, the list as the phone and VoiceOver alternative) is as described for gantt-timeline. Experimental because MonarchGanttTimeline is experimental and no Rook iOS app has adopted it; the API is plain public, not behind an SPI. Several closures are optional (onChange, onOpen). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onChange.
accessibility: Each bar is one element read as "<project>, <start> to <end>, <n>% complete"; with onOpen it is a button with a touch area at least 44 points wide and as tall as the row.
Health is written as words ("On track", "At risk", "Off track", "No health reported") in the row heading, never shown by the bar colour alone.
A group heading has the header trait and reads its name, its project count and its health.
Without onChange bars have no VoiceOver actions; with onChange they offer the timeline's six move and resize actions (the drag equivalent) and every change is announced.
The chart and the list are containers named "Roadmap" for VoiceOver, and the row header says "Project", both replaceable through timelineLabels.
Project names stay at the leading edge in right-to-left layouts, and headings wrap at every Dynamic Type size without cutting text.
edgeCases: A project without dates stays in its group as a "No dates" row; a project with only one date is a one-day marker.
A group with no projects says "0 projects"; a groupID that matches no group puts the project after the groups.
Without progressText and health a project heading has no second line.
An explicit tone always wins over the health tint.
Callbacks receive the MonarchRoadmapItem value the app passed; with duplicate ids the first project is reported.
The roadmap maps the projects again on every render; the mapping is linear in the number of projects.

examples.title: Projects by initiative
examples.template:
MonarchRoadmap(
    [
        MonarchRoadmapItem(
            id: {{items.0.id}},
            label: {{items.0.label}},
            start: {{items.0.start|date}},
            end: {{items.0.end|date}},
            groupID: {{items.0.groupId}},
            progress: {{items.0.progress}} / 100,
            progressText: {{items.0.progressText}},
            health: {{items.0.health|case}}
        ),
        MonarchRoadmapItem(
            id: {{items.1.id}},
            label: {{items.1.label}},
            start: {{items.1.start|date}},
            end: {{items.1.end|date}},
            groupID: {{items.1.groupId}},
            progress: {{items.1.progress}} / 100,
            progressText: {{items.1.progressText}},
            health: {{items.1.health}}
        ),
        MonarchRoadmapItem(
            id: {{items.2.id}},
            label: {{items.2.label}},
            start: {{items.2.start|date}},
            end: {{items.2.end|date}},
            groupID: {{items.2.groupId}},
            progress: {{items.2.progress}} / 100,
            progressText: {{items.2.progressText}},
            health: {{items.2.health|case}}
        ),
        MonarchRoadmapItem(
            id: {{items.3.id}},
            label: {{items.3.label}},
            start: {{items.3.start|date}},
            end: {{items.3.end|date}},
            groupID: {{items.3.groupId}},
            progress: {{items.3.progress}} / 100,
            progressText: {{items.3.progressText}},
            health: {{items.3.health|case}}
        ),
        MonarchRoadmapItem(id: {{items.4.id}}, label: {{items.4.label}}, progressText: {{items.4.progressText}}),
    ],
    state: .constant(MonarchGanttTimelineState(start: {{defaultStart|date}}, zoom: .quarter)),
    groups: [
        MonarchRoadmapGroup(id: {{groups.0.id}}, label: {{groups.0.label}}, start: {{groups.0.start|date}}, end: {{groups.0.end|date}}, health: {{groups.0.health|case}}),
        MonarchRoadmapGroup(id: {{groups.1.id}}, label: {{groups.1.label}}, start: {{groups.1.start|date}}, end: {{groups.1.end|date}}, health: {{groups.1.health|case}}),
    ],
    dependencies: [MonarchGanttTimelineDependency(id: {{dependency.id}}, from: {{dependency.from}}, to: {{dependency.to}})],
    milestones: [MonarchGanttTimelineMilestone(id: {{milestone.id}}, label: {{milestone.label}}, date: {{milestone.date|date}}, itemID: {{milestone.itemId}})],
    today: {{today|date}},
    onOpen: { _ in /* The app opens the project here. */ }
)
.environment(\.calendar, calendar)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "en-GB"))
